newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industrial production falls in August - IBGE.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industrial production falls in August - IBGE.

text.p: Brazilian industrial production in August fell 0.8 percent from July, but grew 5.6 percent in comparison with August 1995, the government's National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said.
The IBGE said with these figures the cumulative indices continued to show a recovery in industrial output.

Industrial production fell 1.5 percent in the period from January to August, compared with a 2.6 percent decline in the January to July period. In the 12 months to August, industrial output fell 3.2 percent as opposed to 4.1 percent in the 12 months to July.
"This recovery is based on an increase in the demand for consumer goods, especially durable goods," the IBGE said in a statement.

Output in August fell in 10 of the 20 industrial sectors covered in the IBGE survey, with electrical and communications materials decreasing 4.4 percent and mineral extraction falling 6 percent, the IBGE said.
Meanwhile, non-metal minerals expanded 3 percent, textiles grew 1.4 percent and clothing increased 2.5 percent.
Production of semi- and non-durable consumer goods expanded 0.4 percent in August from July, but output of durable consumer goods fell 4.3 percent, the IBGE said.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
